recentItems.title: We Need 25 Year Olds Running Congress, Not 85
recentItems.description:
As Mitch McConnell returns to Washington this week and shocks the world with scenes of what can only be described as "elder abuse," I have never been more excited about seeing younger people run for Congress.

Michael Alfonso is running to be the youngest person ever elected to the United States House of Representatives in Wisconsin, and his wife Evita Duffy-Alfonso is often found on the campaign trail right alongside him with their brand-new-baby in tow.

We sat down with Michael & Evita last week at the RNC to talk about the issues young Americans actually care about: affording a home, finding a job that can support a family, pro-family policies, motherhood, and whether Republicans can deliver for the next generation. 

Washington desperately needs young leaders who understand what young families are facing—and Michael and Evita are ready to step into the fight.

recentItems.title: Will There Be Another 9/11 In America? I Asked A CIA Analyst
recentItems.description:
Former CIA officer Sarah Adams joins me for an important conversation about how the threat of terrorism has evolved—and why she believes America may not be prepared for what comes next.

Drawing on her years working in counterterrorism, including her service in Benghazi, Sarah breaks down the connections between groups such as al-Qaeda and ISIS, the possibility of extremist cells operating inside the United States, and the warning signs she believes our government is overlooking.

We also talk about political violence, radicalization through social media, the growing influence of Islamist organizations in the West, and the women living under Taliban rule who are risking everything to tell their stories.

It’s a difficult conversation, but one we can’t afford to avoid.

recentItems.title: Are young Americans being displaced by foreigners in college?
recentItems.description:
The outrage over this tweet is missing the point entirely.

Today, 30+% of graduate students at UT Austin are international. That jumps to more than 60% for engineering students. At an elite, public, AMERICAN university your AMERICAN tax dollars fund... taking spaces from hardworking American engineering students.

Across the 8 campuses of the Ivy League, 25+% of all students (undergrad & grad) are international. At Harvard's Kennedy School of Government, more than 50% of students are not American citizens. Columbia's entire student population is made up of 40% foreigners, and in 5 of their professional and graduate schools, more than 50% of students are foreign nationals.

It is not racist to believe that hardworking American students should be prioritized for positions at American universities and workplaces over foreigners--especially as your tax dollars and government grants you already paid for fund these institutions.

& the failure of FAR too many people in politics to realize this or just run to assume it's somehow a "white supremacist" talking point will prove to be a MASSIVE problem in upcoming elections.

& no... wearing a cowboy hat & cheering at an American football game doesn't mean you've fully assimilated into life as an American citizen.

recentItems.title: How Charlie Kirk Forever Changed Generation Z
recentItems.description:
It has been one year without my friend Charlie Kirk. After considering how best to honor his legacy, there was only one clear answer: talking to college students.

I'm joined by three Turning Point USA chapter leaders to discuss how Charlie changed their lives, inspired a generation to return to faith, and transformed conservative activism on college campuses.

As the darkness grows louder, these students are picking up the torch, defending truth, and continuing Charlie’s mission. We miss him terribly—but we will never stop fighting for the future he believed in. Please pray for these college students as they fight the good fight every day.
